description: AURAS is a collaborative team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We aim to develop an innovative solution for harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire hotspot data to improve the understanding and visualization of fire activity. We welcome enthusiastic team members interested in programming, web development, data analysis, visualization, and environmental science. Join us to collaborate, learn, and build a meaningful technology-driven solution!
summary: FireWatch is a web-based platform designed to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS satellite active fire hotspot data into a unified system for monitoring global burning activity. The platform aims to overcome differences between satellite sensors by standardizing fire observations and organizing them into a consistent spatial and temporal dataset. Users can explore historical fire patterns through an interactive map, a burning activity calendar, and visual analytics that compare fire activity across different regions and time periods. The system also highlights unusual increases in hotspot activity by comparing current observations with historical patterns. By transforming complex satellite observations into accessible and meaningful insights, FireWatch supports early awareness, wildfire monitoring, and informed decision-making. It is designed to assist emergency responders, scientists, environmental researchers, and land managers in identifying critical fire periods, understanding long-term burning trends, and improving fire management strategies.
details:
FireWatch: Harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS Satellite Data for Global Fire Activity Monitoring

FireWatch is a web-based platform designed to bring MODIS and VIIRS satellite active-fire observations together into a common format for easier visualization and analysis.

The platform aims to help users explore fire activity across different locations and time periods using interactive maps, daily fire activity calendars, and historical data visualizations. By combining observations from two satellite sources, FireWatch helps users understand fire patterns and compare the information provided by different satellite sensors.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

  • Makes satellite fire observations easier to explore and understand.
  • Helps identify geographical and temporal patterns in fire activity.
  • Supports awareness of wildfire activity and potential environmental risks.
  • Provides an accessible way for students, researchers, and interested users to explore satellite fire data.

Tools and Technologies:

  • Programming Language: Python
  • Framework: Streamlit
  • Data Processing: Pandas
  • Visualization: Plotly
  • Data Sources: NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS active-fire datasets.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative aspect of FireWatch is its focus on bringing observations from two different satellite systems into one accessible visualization platform. Instead of examining separate datasets independently, users can explore their observations through a unified interface while retaining information about their original satellite sources.

The project considers differences in satellite observations, data quality, spatial resolution, timestamps, and the importance of avoiding misleading duplicate fire counts.

FireWatch aims to make satellite-based fire monitoring more understandable, accessible, and useful for environmental awareness and further research.
